 Order

This revision petition is filed by the complainant in C.C. No. 1810 of 2013 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate-II, Attingal against the order dated 22.06.2020 in C.M.P. No. 1259 of 2019.

2. The case of the complainant is that on 07.09.2008, along with his mother, he reached Killimanoor Police Station for filing a complaint that his wife is missing and at that time, the Sub Inspector was not there and thereafter, around 6.30 p.m., the Sub Inspector reached the Police Station.

It is alleged that the Sub Inspector, after reading the complaint, uttered obscene words against the complainant and his mother and thereafter, beat the complainant on both sides of the cheek and also hit him with hand on his chest.
3. When his mother cried aloud, the Sub Inspector uttered obscene words and also pushed her down.

The Sub Inspector also 2026:KER:25102 wrongfully restrained the complainant and his mother in the room of the Sub Inspector and thereafter, a Police Constable by name Hussain addressed them in obscene words and forcibly took them out of the Police Station and pushed them to the ground.
It is stated that the complainant and his mother subsequently availed treatment from Chirayinkeezhu Taluk Hospital.

The Sub Inspector is arrayed as the first accused and the Police Constable, Muhammad Hussain, as the second accused and they are alleged to have committed the offences under Sections 294(b), 323, 341 and 354 r/w 34 IPC.
4.

After the appearance of the accused persons on summons, they filed C.M.P. No. 1259 of 2019 seeking discharge under Section 245 Cr.P.C stating that on the basis of the statement of the wife of the complainant, the Sub Inspector has registered a case under Section 498A IPC against the complainant and because of that enmity, the accused persons are falsely implicated in this case.

It is also contended that the alleged incident occurred, while the accused were discharging their official duties and therefore, sanction under Section 197 Cr.P.C is required for taking cognizance against the accused persons.

After hearing both sides and perusing the records, the learned Magistrate arrived at the finding that the accused are entitled to get a valid discharge for want of sanction under Section 197 Cr.P.C.,
in as much as everything has occurred in discharge of the official duties of the accused persons.

2 6.

Heard Sri. Kabil Chandran T., the learned counsel for the revision petitioner/complainant, Sri.
M.R. Sarin, the learned counsel appearing for respondents 2 and 3/accused persons and Smt. Maya M.N., the learned Public Prosecutor.

7. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner argued that the respondents have no case that any crime is registered against the complainant or his mother for any overt act committed by them on 07.09.2008.
The specific case of the revision petitioner/complainant is that he and his mother reached the Police Station for filing a complaint that his wife is missing.

It is also pointed out that in the discharge petition filed by the respondents, the only contention raised is that the respondents registered a case against the complainant herein for the 2026:KER:25102 offence under Section 498A IPC on the basis of the statement of his wife and because of that enmity, the respondents were falsely implicated in this case.
8.

It is pertinent to note that the respondents 2 and 3/accused have no case that the complainant or his mother committed any overact in the Police Station on 07.09.2008 or they used any force against the complainant or his mother to prevent them from committing any crime or overtact in the Police Station.

The learned counsel for the respondent Nos. 2 and 3/accused argued that the respondents are entitled to the protection under Section 197 Cr.P.C., in as much as the alleged occurrence was in the Police Station and they were on official duty at the time of the alleged occurrence.
9. It is well settled that in order to get the protection under Section 197 Cr.P.C, there must be a reasonable connection between the act and the official duty.

A Constitution Bench of the Honourable Supreme Court in Matajog Dobey v. H.C.Bhari (AIR 1956 SC 44), held that the offence alleged to have been committed must have something 2026:KER:25102 to do, or must be related in some manner, with the discharge of official duty and no question of sanction can arise under Section 197 Cr.P.C, unless the act complained of is of an offence and the only point to determine is whether it was committed in the discharge of official duty.
10.

In Pukhraj v. State of Rajasthan and another [(1973) 2 SCC 701], the Honourable Supreme Court held that the test appears to be not that the offence is capable of being committed only by a public servant and not by anyone else, but that it is committed by a public servant in an act done or purporting to be done in the execution of duty.
11.

entities.text: Pukhraj v. State of Rajasthan and another [(1973) 2 SCC 701]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In Rakesh Kumar Mishra v. State of Bihar and others [(2006) 1 SCC 557], the Honourable Supreme Court held that Section 197 Cr.P.C has to be construed strictly, while determining its applicability to any act or omission in the course of service and its operation has to be limited to those duties which are discharged in the course of duty.
12.

entities.text: Rakesh Kumar Mishra v. State of Bihar and others [(2006) 1 SCC 557]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As noticed earlier, there is nothing on record to show that any crime is registered against the complainant or his mother for any 2026:KER:25102 overtact committed by them in the Police Station on 07.09.2008 and the respondents 2 and 3 have also no case that the complainant or his mother prevented them from discharging their official duty.

Nazimudeen vs State Of Kerala on 23 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24385792/
3 13.

The specific allegation in the complaint is that respondent Nos. 2 and 3 brutally assaulted the complainant and his mother without any provocation from their part, when they reached the Police Station to file a complaint and the acts alleged against respondent Nos. 2 and 3/accused cannot be treated as acts in discharge of their official duty and they cannot reasonably claim that what they did was by virtue of their official duty and therefore, the findings in the impugned order that they are entitled to the protection under Section 197 Cr.P.C is liable to be set aside.
14.

In the result, this revision petition is allowed and the order dated 22.06.2020 in C.M.P. No. 1259 of 2020 in C.C. No. 1810 of 2013 of the Judicial First Class Magistrate-II, Attingal is set aside and the complaint is restored to file.

The parties are directed to appear before the Judicial First Class Magistrate-II, Attingal on 20.04.2026 and the 2026:KER:25102 learned Magistrate is directed to proceed with the complaint against the accused persons/respondent Nos. 2 and 3 as per law and dispose of the matter as expeditiously as possible.
